inferred.source: surplus copy of a card already seen (190031 and 190933), after the nearest list's other leftover (a second Swablu) was refused
inferred.reason: Least helpful legal filler: a duplicate Stadium is dead once one is in play or the opponent's is out (as in 190933), and it was never needed for a result (190031 lethal did not need the +10); the nearest list's second Swablu was refused because it would make 190933's Copycat shuffle of his only Swablu look safer (chance of redrawing a Swablu among Copycat's 4 cards about 36% with one Swablu vs about 62% with two), and Field Blower / Small Balloon / Igglybuff copies were refused because those cards were decisive or praised in the accepted reviews.

caveats: APPROXIMATE. The cards seen are lower bounds (the packets' own wording); 18 of 20 slots are directly seen, 2 are inferred. All 18 seen cards come from 190933 alone; 190031 adds no extra copies. The 2 never-seen cards are simply the last two cards of the deck in a 10-turn game, so they are random among the list's remainder, not a signal.

decks/dustin and decks/brews contain no Altaria list (their nearest Darkrai lists are Dark-type Hoopa/Absol decks, which this Psychic Energy deck cannot be). The nearest list used is therefore decks/research/altaria.txt, a Limitless-era list (consistency doc: 'Ladder record: Limitless ~53%'), i.e. the current archetype list. It is used only as a template for plausible fillers, never as proof of what Dustin played. It happens to contain exactly the same 13 card names as were seen (and none other), which makes it plausible, but the Aug 29 jlng and Sep 10 Lanora variants of the archetype differ (Cyrus instead of Field Blower; 1 Swablu and 2 Igglybuff in the Lanora list), so the 2 flex slots are genuinely open.

SENSITIVITY: if Dustin's actual list was the research/altaria.txt list, the two inferred slots would be a second Swablu and a second Copycat (the list would then be exactly 2 Swablu + 2 Copycat + 1 Training Area). This reconstruction deliberately does NOT use the second Swablu (see the Training Area reason). Swapping Training Area for Swablu (decks/research/altaria.txt) is the one sensitivity run worth doing if an early-game position (190933 T3, the Copycat turn) is ever used.

Neither inferred card is a key attacker, evolution piece, Poke Ball or search card, by design (conservative direction). A second Copycat gives the pilot a little more draw; the second Training Area is close to a dead card.

Printings: Pokemon ids are the first printing whose HP and attack names match the reviews (Igglybuff 30 HP Sleepy Lullaby, Darkrai 100 HP Bad Dreams, Eevee 50 HP Stampede, Swablu 50 HP Sing, Mega Altaria ex 190 HP Mega Harmony, Espeon 90 HP Hypnoblast). Poke Ball and Professor's Research use the P-A 005 / P-A 007 printings every repo list and example position uses (same card text as the first-listed A2b 111 / A4b 373); the Pokemon-art printings cannot be told apart in the recordings.
Energy type Psychic comes from the Energy Zone in both recordings (190031 TURN_LEDGER T1 energy_zone.next = Psychic; 190933 Psychic Energy attached T3/T5/T7/T9).

Pooling rests on the group note (two recordings 10 minutes apart, same deck name in the Ladder history table). The recordings do not contradict each other, but they cannot prove it; Small Balloon, Training Area and Field Blower each appear in both with no conflict.

Quirk to know: 190933 T3 Copycat shuffled Eevee and Swablu away; with Swablu at one copy this line is riskier in the simulated deck than it may have been for Dustin if he ran two. That is the cost of the conservative choice.
